title: Messages Count in Local Folder Went To Zero When  I  Changed That Folders Title
creator: alank5
content:
9/21/26

Dear T-bird Community Helpers, 

      This is my 1st use of any Mozilla mutual help community message board. I'm learning the ropes. 
      Re. the OS build: I never use beta anything. I established the folder, that went zero on me, recently (less than 2 weeks ago).  I hadn't yet backed it up onto the cloud or a flash drive or other medium. Was just about to, but thought I'd rename the folder 1st,  9/13.      
      My mistake there, but not in the renaming. Never renamed a T-bird folder before. I had set up Thunderbird the week before 9/13, as a backup to e-mails in my Earthlink WebMail Premium account.      1st as a POP account, then later that week, after checking with a reputable AI interface, I made an IMAP.  
      Today I couldn't find any prior messages in this community board. That I, with my best focus, found relevant to my situation.  
      I try to learn what is involved, first, in decisions between products, accounts, and methods to follow. But I don't have all day. I don't short-shrift research, but I don't have all day.  I relied on an AI bot when I had second thoughts on appropriateness of POP account, and it recommended IMAP account be added. Not substituted for the POP one, though---I asked it about that. too. 
      I work hard to learn computer terms but am not deeply skilled with computer stuff.  I cannot generally read between the lines, to infer what sub-step to take to make the next listed step likelier to work. Nor can I understand very unnecessarily complex instructions, so please be feasibly simple in how you instruct me to find a way to restore my local folder. I don't know the exact name it had before. I use spelling tricks to keep folder names short, so there are MANY possibilities for the old name of that folder. 
      Your advice, please. I will be grateful for friendly, complete, instructions. Worded simply as is feasible.  And questions 1st, sure, if you need to know more 1st. 
         Thank You,              AK
